items.title: Classes and Objects – Representing Real-World Entities in Code

source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Classes and Objects under 3.2, with Figure 3.1, the Student example and its printed notes (PDF 38, printed 34).

blocks.text: A class is a blueprint or template that defines the properties (attributes) and actions (methods) of an entity. An object is an instance of a class that holds actual values for its attributes (as shown in Figure 3.1). Classes and objects allow programmers to model real-world entities in code. Using classes and objects helps organize data and related functionality together, making programs more structured.

blocks.alt: Class and object diagram: a box Class: Person lists Attributes (name, age, gender) and Methods (eat(), sleep(), work()) beside a person silhouette. Arrows lead to Object P1 (name = Bob, age = 34, gender = Male; eat(), sleep(), work()) with a picture of a man, and Object P2 (name = Jenny, age = 27, gender = Female; eat(), sleep(), work()) with a picture of a woman.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.1: Diagram Showing Class and Object relationship (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.1).

blocks.text:
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def display(self):
        print("Student Name:", self.name)

# Creating objects
object1 = Student("Ali")
object2 = Student("Ahmed")

# Using objects
object1.display()
object2.display()

items: class Student → defines a blueprint for students
__init__ → sets the name when an object is created
object1 and object2 → two different student objects
Each object has its own data (Ali, Ahmed)
